citations.quote: Define the supersymmetry generators on $\mathscr S$ by

The supercharges $Q_\alpha,\bar Q_{\dot\alpha}$ anticommute with each $\bar D_{\dot\beta}$, so the defined supersymmetry transformation preserves chirality and induces a unique smooth component transformation.

For one generator, write a polynomial uniquely with that generator on the left as $f=f_0+\xi_i f_1$, with $f_0,f_1$ independent of $\xi_i$, and define its Berezin integral by the complex-linear coefficient-extraction rule $\int d\xi_i\,f=f_1$. Thus $\int d\xi_i\,1=0$ and $\int d\xi_i\,\xi_i=1$. Fix the ordered measures
$$ \int d^2\theta:=\int d\theta^2\,d\theta^1,\qquad \int d^2\bar\theta:=\int d\bar\theta^{\dot2}\,d\bar\theta^{\dot1},\qquad \int d^4\theta:=\int d\bar\theta^{\dot2}\,d\bar\theta^{\dot1}\,d\theta^2\,d\theta^1. $$
With this order, $\int d^4\theta$ extracts the coefficient of $\theta^1\theta^2\bar\theta^{\dot1}\bar\theta^{\dot2}$. For superspace coordinates $x=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)\in\mathbb R^{1,3}$ in natural units $\hbar=c=1$, assign mass dimensions $[x^\mu]=-1$, $[\theta^\alpha]=[\bar\theta^{\dot\alpha}]=-\tfrac12$, $[d\theta^\alpha]=[d\bar\theta^{\dot\alpha}]=\tfrac12$, and hence $[d^2\theta]=[d^2\bar\theta]=1$ and $[d^4\theta]=2$. These are formal engineering dimensions; no physical model or empirical unit convention is asserted.

Berezin total derivatives have zero top coefficient and the compact-support spacetime divergence contributes no boundary term.

Choose a specified set $I$ of representation labels and, for each $a\in I$, a finite-dimensional complex vector space $V_a$, a positive-definite Hermitian form $h_a$, and a smooth group homomorphism $\rho_a:G\to U(V_a,h_a)$. Here $U(V_a,h_a)$ is the group of complex-linear isometries of $h_a$, and a representation is the corresponding finite-dimensional group action. Its associated vector bundle is the quotient $E_a=P\times_{\rho_a}V_a$ with relation $[pg,v]=[p,\rho_a(g)v]$.

The connection-normalized fields are $A_\mu=-ig_{\mathrm{YM}}B_\mu$, $\lambda=g_{\mathrm{YM}}\lambda_B$, and $D=g_{\mathrm{YM}}D_B$; hence $[A_\mu]=1$, $[\lambda]=3/2$, and $[D]=2$. The full prepotential is used for supersymmetry transformations; Wess–Zumino gauge is only a component representative and need not be preserved by an uncompensated supersymmetry variation.
The matter covariant derivative is $D_\mu\phi^a=\partial_\mu\phi^a+\rho_{a*}(A_\mu)\phi^a=\partial_\mu\phi^a-ig B_\mu^b t_{b,a}\phi^a$, where $t_{b,a}=i\rho_{a*}(T_b)$ and $T_b=-i\sigma_b/2$.
